title: Shell & POSIX utilities
summary: /bin/sh and the POSIX utilities found through PATH behave as POSIX.1-2024's Shell and Utilities volume specifies: the shell language, file, text and process utilities, and whole real-world scripts run as files.

cases.title: Single quotes keep every character literally, including $ and double quotes
Double quotes expand parameters but keep \$, \", \\ and single quotes literal
${x:-word} substitutes for unset or empty, ${x-word} only for unset
${#x} expands to the length of x in characters
${x#p}, ${x##p}, ${x%p} and ${x%%p} remove the shortest and longest matching prefix and suffix
$(...) and backquotes substitute a command's output with trailing newlines removed
$((...)) evaluates C integer arithmetic with precedence, %, shifts, and hex and octal constants
Field splitting on a non-whitespace IFS keeps empty fields between delimiters
Pathname expansion matches *, ? and [!...] against the directory, sorted
Pathname expansion applies to parameter expansion results, which are not expanded again
A here-document with an unquoted delimiter expands parameters and commands and honours \$
With set -C, > refuses to overwrite an existing file and >| overwrites it
2>&1 sends standard error to where standard output goes
A pipeline connects stdout to stdin and its status is the last command's
! inverts a pipeline's exit status
&& runs on success, || on failure, with equal precedence left to right
if, elif and else run the branch of the first true condition
case matches patterns with *, |, bracket classes and the empty string, in order
for iterates over a word list, and over "$@" when in is left out
while loops while its condition succeeds and until while it fails
A function gets its own positional parameters and the caller's are restored
return n sets a function's status, and without return it is the last command's
$# counts, "$@" keeps each parameter and "$*" joins them with the first IFS character
$$ is the shell's PID in subshells too, and $! names the last background job for wait
set -e exits on a failing command but not in an if condition, an || list or after !
set -u makes expanding an unset parameter an error that exits, but ${x-word} is allowed
set -f disables pathname expansion and set +f restores it
export passes a variable to child processes, and an assignment prefix only to that command
Assigning to a readonly variable is an error that exits the (sub)shell
unset removes a variable and unset -f a function
shift n drops the first n positional parameters
eval joins its arguments and runs them as a command
exec with a command replaces the shell, so later commands never run
A trap on EXIT runs when the shell exits and keeps the exit status
A trap on a signal runs its action when the shell receives the signal
exit n ends the shell with status n, and a subshell's exit ends only the subshell
. runs a file in the current shell, and return in it ends the file with a status
cd changes the directory and PWD, pwd agrees, and cd to a missing directory fails
A command killed by a signal has exit status 128 plus the signal number
( ) runs in a subshell whose changes do not persist, while { } runs in the current shell
alias defines a word later commands expand, alias NAME writes it for reuse, and unalias removes it
ls lists a directory's names sorted, one per line when stdout is not a terminal, without dot files
ls -a includes . , .. and names starting with a period
ls -d lists a directory operand itself rather than its contents
ls -l shows the mode string, link count, size and name of a file
ls -ld shows a directory's type and permission bits
cp copies a file's contents to a new file
cp -R copies a directory hierarchy
cp of a directory without -R writes a diagnostic and exits non-zero
cp -p preserves the file's modification time and permission bits
mv moves a file into another directory
mv renames a directory together with its contents
rm -r removes a directory hierarchy
rm of a missing file writes a diagnostic and exits non-zero
rm -f of a missing file is silent and exits 0
mkdir -p creates missing parents and accepts directories that exist
rmdir removes an empty directory
rmdir of a directory that is not empty fails and leaves it
ln makes a hard link that shares the file's contents and raises its link count
ln -s makes a symbolic link that reads through to its target
chmod with an octal mode sets the permission bits
chmod with a symbolic mode adds, removes and sets bits per class
touch creates an empty file that does not exist
touch -t sets a file's modification time, which ls -l shows
A file touched with an older time is older than a new file to test -nt and -ot
find -name matches file names against a pattern throughout the tree
find -type d selects directories, including the starting point
find -mtime +n selects files modified more than n days ago
find -exec runs a command for each file with {} replaced by its path
find -exec ... {} + runs the command once with all the paths, and find fails when it fails
find -prune keeps find from descending into a directory
du writes one line per directory in the hierarchy, ending with the operand
df -k -P writes the POSIX header and a line for the file system holding the operand
test's -e, -f, -d, -s, -r, -w, -x and -h operators describe files
[ found through PATH evaluates its expression and requires the closing ]
basename strips the directory and a suffix, and handles / and trailing slashes
dirname strips the last component, giving . for a bare name and / for /
readlink writes the contents of a symbolic link
realpath resolves . , .. and symbolic links to an absolute path
cat concatenates files and - for standard input in order
head -n 2 writes the first two lines
head -c 5 writes the first five bytes
tail -n 2 writes the last two lines
wc counts lines, words and bytes, in that order
sort orders lines by byte value in the POSIX locale
sort -n orders by numeric value, including negative numbers
sort -r reverses the order
sort -k 2,2n sorts numerically on the second field
sort -u writes one line of each run of equal lines
uniq -c precedes each line with the number of times it occurred
cut -d : -f 1,3 selects fields by delimiter
cut -c 2-4 selects a range of characters
tr a-z A-Z translates a range of characters
tr -d deletes the characters in a set
tr -s squeezes repeated characters to one
sed s/// replaces the first match, and with g every match
sed -n prints only what p prints, with $ addressing the last line
sed 2,3d deletes a range of lines
awk -F splits fields at the separator and sets NF
awk runs an action only for records its pattern selects
awk runs BEGIN before input and END after it, with NR counting records
awk printf formats %5.2f, %-3s, %d and %x
grep -E matches extended regular expressions with alternation and grouping
grep -v writes the lines that do not match
grep -c writes the number of matching lines
grep -l writes the names of the files that contain a match
grep -n precedes each matching line with its line number
grep -i matches without regard to case
grep exits 1 when nothing matches and more than 1 for a missing file
diff of identical files writes nothing and exits 0
diff writes the default change format and exits 1 when files differ
diff -c writes both file names and the context format, marking changed lines with !
diff -e writes an ed script that edits from the last change back, and -f the forward form
diff -r introduces each differing file with a diff line and names files in one directory only
diff exits above 1 when its output cannot be written or an operand is missing
cmp names the first differing byte and line and exits 1
comm writes lines unique to each file and common lines in three tab-indented columns
paste joins corresponding lines with tabs, and -s -d joins one file's lines
tee copies standard input to standard output and each file, and -a appends
od -A n -t x1 and -t o1 dump bytes in hexadecimal and octal
printf formats %s, %d, %5.2f, %x, %o and %c
echo writes its arguments separated by single spaces and a newline
sleep 1 suspends execution for at least a second
sleep with an operand that is not a number writes a diagnostic and exits non-zero
kill -l names the signal for a number and for an exit status above 128
kill sends SIGTERM by default, and wait reports 128 plus 15
kill -s KILL sends the named signal
kill -0 tests that a process exists without signalling it
wait with no operands waits for every background job and returns 0
wait with a PID returns that job's exit status
A command ended with & runs in the background while the shell goes on
Without job control a background command's standard input is /dev/null
ps -o pid= -p lists the shell's own PID
ps -o comm= names the command a process runs
ps -A lists every process, the shell included
ps rejects an empty -p list, fails when it selects nothing, selects by real user, and writes four columns by default
nohup runs a command with SIGHUP ignored
env NAME=value adds the variable to the environment of the command it runs
env -i starts from an empty environment
nice -n 5 runs a command at a niceness raised by 5
timeout ends a command that runs too long with status 124 and passes on a quick one's status
timeout -s KILL sends the named signal and exits 128 plus its number
timeout passes SIGTERM it receives on to the command and exits with the command's status
timeout -k sends SIGKILL after a fractional limit even when the timeout signal is SIGALRM
true found through PATH exits 0
false found through PATH exits non-zero
xargs passes words from standard input as arguments
xargs -n 2 passes at most two arguments per command
xargs -I replaces a string with each whole input line
id -u writes a numeric user ID and id writes uid= with it
uname writes the system name, the same as uname -s, and uname -a starts with it
date +format expands %Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S and %% from the current time
expr evaluates integer arithmetic with *, /, % and negative operands
expr string : regex writes the \( \) match or the length matched
expr exits 1 when the result is zero or null and 0 otherwise
test compares integers with -eq, -ne, -gt, -ge, -lt and -le
test found through PATH exits 1 when its integer comparison is false
umask sets the mask new files are created under, and umask -S writes it symbolically
getconf writes ARG_MAX of at least 4096 and a PATH that finds the standard utilities
getconf answers option, limits.h, processor and programming-environment names, and -v rejects an unsupported environment
command -v writes the path of a utility, the name of a built-in or function, and fails for neither
time -p runs a command, writes real, user and sys times to stderr and exits with its status
time -p exits 128 plus the signal number when a signal ends the command
tty with standard input that is not a terminal writes not a tty and exits 1
free, a legacy /bin name, reports the same total memory as /proc/meminfo
A tr | sort | uniq -c | sort | head pipeline lists the three most frequent words
The word-frequency pipeline takes the number of words to list as an argument
The word-frequency pipeline reads standard input when its file operand is -
A configure-style probe finds tools with command -v and writes config.h
The configure probe takes --prefix=DIR into config.h
The configure probe rejects an unknown option on stderr with status 1 and writes nothing
A make-free build loop compiles every source into out/
The build loop rebuilds only the object older than its source
The build loop stops with set -e when a step fails
A log rotator moves the log to .1 and leaves an empty log
Rotating three times keeps only the newest KEEP old logs
The log rotator reports a missing log on stderr and exits 1
An awk CSV report totals quantity and revenue per region and overall
The CSV report of a file with only a header has no regions and a zero total
A recursive shell function walks a directory tree depth first
The tree walker keeps names with spaces intact
The tree walker lists a symbolic link to a directory without following it
A here-document template expands variables, a loop's output and arithmetic
A script written from a quoted here-document keeps its $ references for when it runs
getopts parses flags and option-arguments, and shift leaves the operands
getopts takes grouped flags and stops at --
getopts reports an unknown option and the script exits 2 with its usage
getopts reports an option missing its argument and the script exits 2 with its usage
An EXIT trap removes the script's temporary directory when it ends normally
The EXIT trap runs on exit 3 and the script keeps status 3
On SIGINT the INT trap exits 130 and the EXIT trap still cleans up
A script sources a library file found next to it and calls its functions
A library's die function writes to stderr and exits the sourcing script with 1
The script finds its library through $0 when run from another directory
